nodes.label: DisasmStudio
nodes.rationale: Purpose: make an unfamiliar binary understandable quickly. Built as a real tool, not a mockup — static disassembly and a live Win32 debugger unified in one fast, self-contained C++20/ImGui/D3D11 workbench.

nodes.label: Fixed Single-Window Browser-Style Tab UI
nodes.rationale: No docking, by deliberate design: a fixed, predictable browser-style layout with a top tab strip; io.IniFilename = nullptr so no layout persistence.

nodes.label: No Scripting/Plugin API (Explicit Non-Goal)
nodes.rationale: The user explicitly does not want a scripting/plugin API. The product is the curated, hand-built workbench, not an extension platform — tabs are compiled in, no extension point exists.

nodes.label: Static Self-Contained Single-EXE Build
nodes.rationale: x64-windows-static vcpkg triplet + static CRT (/MT) links all deps and the runtime into one DisasmStudio.exe — no installer, no VC++ Redistributable, no side-by-side DLLs (only the OS's d3dcompiler_47.dll).

nodes.label: GPU-Accelerated Clipper-Rendered UI
nodes.rationale: Spec constraint: must be fast and 3D/GPU-accelerated. Hardware D3D11 device (WARP only as graceful degrade), vsync-capped, occlusion-aware frame skipping, every large list clipper-rendered up to ~800k instructions.

nodes.label: Dependency-Light / Hand-Rolled Subsystems
nodes.rationale: Where a dependency would add weight or risk, the project hand-rolls a focused replacement: its own JSON library, its own decompiler, its own capability scanner. Only ImGui/Zydis/Capstone/Keystone are third-party.

nodes.label: Heuristic Honesty Rule (Confidence + Evidence)
nodes.rationale: Never present guesses as facts: every heuristic note/finding carries confidence + evidence + analyzer name, guesses render amber with reason tooltips, are never persisted, and a user rename always wins.

nodes.label: Content-Hash-Keyed Project Persistence
nodes.rationale: Analysis follows the bytes, not the path: a 64-bit FNV-1a content hash keys the JSON sidecar in %APPDATA%/DisasmStudio/projects/<hash>.json; addresses stored as hex strings for exact 64-bit round-trip; hand-rolled JSON.

nodes.label: Background Analysis Service (Worker Thread + Epoch)
nodes.rationale: Heavy load-time passes (function discovery + naming, string scan) run off the render thread. Invariants: worker builds its own decoder, every load/patch bumps an epoch so stale results are dropped, and cancelAndWaitIdle precedes any image realloc.

nodes.label: Patch-List Order = Application Order Invariant
nodes.rationale: Overlapping patches resolve later-wins; each patch's orig is captured as PRISTINE bytes via SubstitutePristine, revert re-applies surviving overlappers in order, and buildPatchedImage splices in the same order — never re-sort the patch list.

nodes.label: Lightweight In-House Decompiler
nodes.rationale: A 'good enough to read' structurer, deliberately not a full decompiler (no SSA, no global type lattice): Cooper/Harvey/Kennedy dominators + post-dominators + natural loops recover if/else and while/do-while with goto fallback; optional data-flow pre-pass names locals and propagates constants; per-line VA source map syncs pseudocode to the listing.

nodes.label: DecompileToPython Display-Side Transform
nodes.rationale: A pure display-side text transform of the pseudo-C: the worker and LRU always hold pseudo-C so language switches stay instant and the C path stays byte-identical; the per-line VA map is preserved through the transform.

nodes.label: Heuristic Function Name Guessing (FunctionNamer)
nodes.rationale: Does what a human RE does on a first pass: thunks → j_<API>, entry → start, stubs → nullsub/ret_zero, API-set evidence → semantic verbs (read_file, inject_thread, encrypt_data), single-API wrappers snake-cased, distinctive embedded identifier strings reused. Guesses flow through symbolFor, are de-duped, toggled, and never persisted.

nodes.label: Per-Function Annotation Engine (FuncAnnotate)
nodes.rationale: x86/x64 heuristics: calling convention + args, stack frame/locals, register lifetimes, plain-language branch meaning, loop pattern scans (XOR-decode/checksum/byte-compare), vtable/this-ptr hints, call-arg sniffing, API-set patterns. Cached in an 8-entry LRU; only the cursor's function builds eagerly so scrolling never builds CFGs.

nodes.label: Java Bytecode Annotation Engine (JvmAnnotate)
nodes.rationale: Per-opcode stack-effect gloss, operand-stack depth via abstract interpretation over the bytecode CFG, branch meaning, call/field/string extraction, API-category findings, and a password/serial/license check-method verdict — same confidence+evidence honesty contract as the native engine.

nodes.label: Java .class Parser (JvmClass)
nodes.rationale: Pure, bounded, unit-tested parser: constant pool, methods + Code attributes at file offsets, LineNumberTable, descriptor pretty-printer. Feeds the JVM disassembler, function seeding, and live JDWP symbolication (ParseConstantPoolOnly).

nodes.label: JVM Debugging over JDWP
nodes.rationale: Pure wire protocol (Core/Jdwp) + Winsock client thread (JdwpClient): attach to running JVMs (HotSpot dynamic-attach injection, no prelaunch flag), breakpoints at (class, method, bci), stepping, live Method::Bytecodes disassembly. Caller-thread requests park on replies; the reader thread uses its own nested pump to avoid deadlock.

nodes.label: Real Win32 Debugger (Core/Debugger)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated debug thread is mandatory because the Win32 debug API requires the attaching thread to service every WaitForDebugEvent; the UI posts commands and reads a lock-guarded DbgSnapshot. SW (0xCC restore→step→re-arm dance) + HW (DR0–DR3) + conditional breakpoints, step into/over/out, WOW64 support, hProcMtx_ closes the handle TOCTOU window.

nodes.label: IDisassembler Engine-Agnostic Interface
nodes.rationale: The rest of the app must never know or care whether an instruction was decoded by Zydis or Capstone: one minimal string-based Instruction struct, four semantic flags + branchTarget as the only signals CFG/xref/call-graph/discovery consume; engines swappable at runtime.

nodes.label: Capstone (Multi-Arch Disassembler Backend)
nodes.rationale: Covers ARM/ARM64/MIPS/PPC/RISC-V (forced for non-x86 by the factory); PPC opened little-endian to match every loadable image; non-x86 returns detected textually because CS_GRP_RET misses them — keeps CFG boundaries and step-out correct.

nodes.label: Keystone (Patch Assembler)
nodes.rationale: Supports only x86/x64/ARM/ARM64 and fails with a clear 'unsupported' message for other arches — disassembly coverage is deliberately broader than assembly coverage.

nodes.label: BinaryFile Multi-Format Loader
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for what the bytes are: PE32/PE32+, ELF, thin Mach-O, Java .class, and raw; magic-sniffed with graceful degrade to Raw on parse failure; arch recovered from the format header (machine()); uniform VA↔offset math; contentHash keys persistence.

nodes.label: ELF/Mach-O imageBase_=0 Convention
nodes.rationale: ELF/Mach-O keep imageBase_=0 and store the absolute VM address in Section::virtualAddress so the shared rva = va - imageBase math handles all formats uniformly — no per-format branch in the hot translation path.

nodes.label: Java .class Identity Mapping (VA == File Offset)
nodes.rationale: Java .class loads use imageBase 0 with every section's virtualAddress == rawOffset so VA == file offset — exactly what JvmDisassembler needs for tableswitch/lookupswitch padding math (pad is relative to method code start, not instruction address).

nodes.label: TechScan Capability Detection
nodes.rationale: Real capability scan over imports (anti-debug/network/crypto/injection), packer section-name signatures (UPX, VMProtect, Themida), and distinctive byte patterns (syscall stubs, AES S-box, SHA-256/MD5 constants) — no fabricated results; a clean binary shows few or none.

nodes.label: Signature Scanning (SigMatch, ?? Wildcards)
nodes.rationale: Masked Boyer-Moore-Horspool byte-pattern search with ?? wildcards; file or live mode (chunked with pattern-1 overlap so straddling matches are never dropped); Sig Health scores saved signatures by real match count.

nodes.label: DbgHelp Process-Global Lock (DbgHelpMutex)
nodes.rationale: DbgHelp is process-global single-threaded; both the UI's SymbolResolver and the debug thread's unwindStack call it on the same handle, so every Sym*/StackWalk64 call must take DbgHelpMutex().

nodes.label: Semantic Theme System (theme::col)
nodes.rationale: Never hardcode RGBA for semantic UI colors — route through theme::col accessors derived from a compact seed Palette so all eight palettes (incl. Light) stay correct on a theme switch; interactive states are accent blends, not per-theme special cases.

nodes.label: Testable Core / Review-Verified UI Strategy
nodes.rationale: Pure-logic Core modules compile standalone (g++ sandbox or MSVC cl) and are unit-tested off-target — the fast verification loop without the 20-40 min app build; ImGui/Win32/engine-facing code cannot compile there and is review-verified via full solution builds.

nodes.label: AMD-V (SVM) Hypervisor Debugging Backend
nodes.rationale: Research-grade, opt-in low-artifact introspection: a hypervisor can observe a target from underneath the OS without the int3 bytes and debug-API artifacts targets can detect. Driver packaging/signing/loading/runtime validation are explicitly out of scope; the app delivers everything without it.

hyperedges.label: Engines Bound by the Confidence+Evidence Honesty Contract
